curriculum.lesson_evidence: Rehearsing a music piece means repeating it to improve. First play it through, then find the tricky part, such as a fast rhythm or a loud-to-soft change. Practise that part slowly, then at the right tempo, and join it back into the piece. Refining means making small changes to improve the sound, such as adjusting the dynamics, balance or tempo. Record what you changed. Keep the volume safe for your ears, rest your voice or hands, and finish by playing the whole piece.

lesson.guided_practice:
PRACTISE BEFORE READING THE FEEDBACK
A group plays well but speeds up in the loud section. Write two steps for fixing the problem and one thing to check afterwards.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Play only that section slowly with a metronome or tapped beat, then speed up gradually. Then play the full piece. Afterwards check that the beat stayed steady.' Isolating the tricky part and checking the result is how to refine.

WATCH FOR
Believing that repeating the whole piece again and again is the best way to rehearse. Focusing on one tricky part, then putting it back, usually works faster.
lesson.independent_task:
INDEPENDENT EVIDENCE
Rehearse a piece for your showcase. Choose one tricky section, practise it slowly and then at full tempo. Record two changes you made to dynamics, tempo or balance, then play the whole piece for family.

Write a short reflection naming one artistic choice you changed and why. Movement or instrument work is optional, adult-supervised and can be described instead.

teach_steps.example:
WORKED MODEL
Example: Kai's group plays 'Rain'. The crescendo in the middle is too sudden. They isolate that part, play it slowly four times with a gradually widening gesture and then speed up. They also lower the drum so the shakers can be heard. They then play the whole piece. Their note: 'Crescendo smoother. Drum softer. Count in properly.'

TRY FIRST
A group plays well but speeds up in the loud section. Write two steps for fixing the problem and one thing to check afterwards.

FEEDBACK
Strong answer: 'Play only that section slowly with a metronome or tapped beat, then speed up gradually. Then play the full piece. Afterwards check that the beat stayed steady.' Isolating the tricky part and checking the result is how to refine.
teach_steps.explain:

Record what you changed. Keep the volume safe for your ears, rest your voice or hands, and finish by playing the whole piece.

WHY IT MATTERS
This helps the learner make intentional visual, music, drama or dance choices and name their effect, rather than saying an artwork is simply “nice”. Keep every claim linked to an element or technique.

teaching.misconception: Repeating the worked example cannot show transfer to a new artwork or performance.
teaching.model: Rehearsing a music piece means repeating it to improve. First play it through, then find the tricky part, such as a fast rhythm or a loud-to-soft change. Practise that part slowly, then at the right tempo, and join it back into the piece. Refining means making small changes to improve the sound, such as adjusting the dynamics, balance or tempo. Record what you changed. Keep the volume safe for your ears, rest your voice or hands, and finish by playing the whole piece. Now choose a different subject or piece to show you can transfer the idea.
